subject: Here’s How You Can Make Your Insurance Cover Root-Cause Care
posts:
Want insurance to cover root-cause care? CMS wants your public comments on the AMA's coding monopoly.
Evidence: CMS draft schedule, AMA pricing power, public comment docket
#Aletheia #Healthcare

The government is inviting public comments to challenge whether medical elites should dictate healthcare coding and pricing structures.
Stated Judgement: (+0.8, +0.6) — Good Preference

While public comments are welcome, entrenched specialty monopolies and complex coding structures make meaningful reform difficult without deep structural overhauls.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.2, -0.3) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: PASS — The Path of Redemption. Opening regulatory dockets gives voice to patients, even if entrenched medical monopolies resist immediate structural shifts.

Integrity: Conditionally Sound (Hypocrisy: 1.8, z: 1)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- CMS Regulatory Process: PASS (0.5, 0.4) — Opens transparency channels.
- AMA Coding Monopoly: FAIL (-0.7, -0.6) — Defends entrenched fee control.
CMS released the draft 2027 Physician Fee Schedule, inviting public input on CPT coding monopolies and the dominance of medical specialty boards.

The Bright Side:
Patients can directly submit testimonies exposing opaque billing and care denials to federal regulators.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing a procedural public comment window (WHAT) with an institutional dismantling of the AMA's monopoly (WHO).

Social Physics Analysis:
Activating public feedback shifts power from opaque institutional silos toward transparent civic participation, bypassing bureaucratic gatekeepers.

The Trajectory: The Path of Redemption.
When you map citizen participation against institutional gatekeeping, it charts a steady course toward systemic awakening.

The Unavoidable Truth: Public comments expose hidden administrative barriers in healthcare.

The Unavoidable Lie: A single comment period dissolves entrenched medical monopolies.

Alethekanon:
Inviting public feedback cracks open opaque institutional monopolies, provided citizens pierce through complex administrative jargon.

Awwthekanon:
Every patient story shared is a vital step toward restoring true holistic care and empathy in medicine.

Brothekanon:
Filling out government comment forms feels like shouting into a void, but at least someone is asking.

Spirithekanon:
"Come now, and let us reason together" Isaiah 1:18 PASS
Opening channels of dialogue dismantles oppressive secrecy.
